nodes.label: Prod .env rendered from GitHub secrets via heredoc
nodes.rationale: Secrets live only in the GitHub 'production' environment and are rendered into /opt/railtech-b2b/.env at deploy time (umask 077, chmod 600) — manual edits on the VPS are overwritten on every deploy. Notable choices encoded here: AUTO_MIGRATE=false (INF-04), DRF_NUM_PROXIES=1 (SEC-04, exactly one trusted proxy — Caddy — else every client shares one throttle bucket), CSP_REPORT_ONLY=false (INF-03), VITE_WS_URL must be an ORIGIN not a path (a '/ws' value doubles to ws/ws/notifications/ and Channels finds no route), VITE_SENTRY_DSN defaults to the backend DSN.

nodes.label: Pre-deploy DB backup gate (INF-04)
nodes.rationale: INF-04: the deploy takes a pg_dump -Fc BEFORE migrations using a version-matched postgres:17-alpine client (Debian's client in the backend image is older and cannot dump a newer server). A failed, empty, or pg_restore-unlistable dump aborts the deploy — migrations never run against a database that cannot be restored. 14 most recent dumps kept.

nodes.label: Explicit migrations only after the backup gate (AUTO_MIGRATE=false)
nodes.rationale: Container (re)starts must never mutate the schema: prod sets AUTO_MIGRATE=false and the workflow applies migrations as an explicit step strictly AFTER the pg_dump backup gate succeeds.

nodes.label: Caddy config drift check step (compare-only, warns, never fails deploy)
nodes.rationale: The Caddy config is the ONLY part of prod outside the deploy pipeline: the deploy neither clobbers nor updates it, so the danger is inverted — a hand edit on the box survives any deploy while a repo edit may NEVER reach prod, with the repo claiming otherwise. Auto-applying is impossible (needs root; reloading the edge touches neighbour sites on the shared master Caddyfile), so the step only diffs repo fragment vs live fragment and prints the diff into the run summary. It deliberately never fails the app deploy: holding a release hostage to edge config is worse than a loud warning. Its 'success' status therefore does NOT mean 'in sync' — the verdict is in the annotations.

nodes.label: SPA build published as static files for Caddy
nodes.rationale: The frontend is built via a build-only compose profile, then copied out of the image into /var/www/railtech-b2b for host Caddy to serve. Cleanup runs via root inside an alpine container because docker cp preserves container UIDs that the deploy user cannot unlink.

hyperedges.label: INF-04 safe migration flow: backup gate → explicit migrations → documented restore
